definition: Policy approaches that focus on regulating or monitoring the computational resources (hardware, training compute) used to develop advanced AI systems.
details: Compute governance treats large-scale training compute as a useful policy lever, since it is a relatively measurable and controllable input to frontier AI development compared to algorithms or data.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. And that is Compute Governance — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
